summary: In an ordinary Cline session, plain code runs the work and sets its limits, and the AI model decides when the task is done. By default the model also writes the summary that replaces older history, and in interactive command-line plan mode it decides when to start acting on the plan.

judgments.question: On the command line, do tool calls run without asking you?
judgments.answer: By default, yes. At startup code sets one policy for all tools from the --auto-approve or --yolo flag if given, else your saved setting, else on, so out of the box tool calls run without asking, in ordinary sessions as well as yolo mode.

judgments.question: In VS Code, may this shell command run?
judgments.answer: When a command reaches the approval step and neither its policy nor the auto-approve toggle for commands (off by default) approves it, code shows an Approve or Reject row and waits for the person. Only Approve lets that command run; a typed message leaves the question open.

judgments.question: In plan mode on the interactive command line, who decides you have approved the plan and the work can start?
judgments.answer: The model, by calling a switch-to-act tool; the tool does not look at what you wrote. When that turn completes, the command-line tool rebuilds the session in act mode and starts on the plan. The call itself follows the command line's approval setting.

judgments.question: How does it decide the task is finished?
judgments.answer: In an ordinary session, the model replies without asking to use a tool and code ends the run as completed; nothing checks that the work was done.

judgments.question: When its yolo mode ends a run as "verified", does anything check?
judgments.answer: No. The model ends the run by submitting a summary with a verified yes or no, and both the command-line tool and scheduled runs accept the submission either way.

judgments.question: Did a scheduled run succeed?
judgments.answer: Unless the run was cancelled, timed out or lost its place, any turn that does not end with an error, including one that ended as stopped, is recorded as done and counted as a success.

judgments.question: How long can it keep going before it is stopped?
judgments.answer: Ordinary VS Code and command-line sessions set no limit on steps. A time limit applies only where a caller sets one, such as the --timeout flag on a one-shot run or a schedule.

judgments.question: When the history gets too long, who decides what to keep?
judgments.answer: With the default strategy, a model writes a summary of the older part while about the last 20,000 tokens stay word for word, and code puts in place any summary that is not empty.

problems.title: Shell commands are cut off at 30 seconds
problems.plain: On the command line, a shell command the agent runs gets 30 seconds by default; then code tries to kill it and the agent is told it timed out, so a long build, test run or install can be stopped partway. Cline's tracker has two open reports about this limit.

verified.claimsPass: an independent AI reviewer from another company (OpenAI Codex, read-only) on 2026-11-08, in four rounds; each sentence it questioned was narrowed, removed or kept with the reason recorded

problems.title: A file edit that timed out can still be written
problems.plain: File edits are given a time limit, but reaching it only tells the model the edit failed; the edit itself is not stopped. So the model can be told an edit timed out while the change still lands in the file. An open report in Cline's tracker describes the same outcome in VS Code: a timeout reported after the write had landed.

verified.claimsPass: an independent AI reviewer from another company (OpenAI Codex, read-only) on 2026-11-08, in four rounds; each sentence it questioned was narrowed, removed or kept with the reason recorded

problems.title: A cut-off summary is used as if it were complete
problems.plain: When the default strategy shortens the history, the model's summary replaces the older messages. If the summary was cut off before the model finished it, code still puts it in place; only an empty reply is skipped.

verified.claimsPass: an independent AI reviewer from another company (OpenAI Codex, read-only) on 2026-11-08, in four rounds; each sentence it questioned was narrowed, removed or kept with the reason recorded

notChecked: This card was taken from the published map of Cline at one commit and covers only decisions shown there. It did not look at Cline's hosted services or at code outside the parts the map covers (its SDK, command line, hub and VS Code extension). One problem was also tested by running it: a file edit that timed out. On 2026-11-12, at this commit, Cline's editor tool was given a 50 ms limit around its real file editor. The test delayed that editor on purpose before it started. The tool reported that the edit had timed out while the file was still unchanged, and the file changed once the editor finished. In separate cases of the same test, a normal edit landed and reported success, and an edit made to fail before writing left the file unchanged. No model was used, and the test does not show how often a real edit is that slow. The reproduction covers only the three cases described here.
